title: Giant Recycled Table Sets World Record
summary:
On September 12, 2026, about 20,000 people gathered in Bucharest, Romania. They shared a meal at a very long table called the "Uniting Table." The table stretched 3.1 miles, or 4.99 kilometers. It set a new Guinness World Record for the longest table made from recycled materials.

But the world record was only part of the goal. A nonprofit group called Bloom The World organized the event. It also raised more than $110,000 for Romania's first psychiatric hospital for children. This is a hospital that provides mental health care.

Children in Bucharest who need this care are currently treated in an old facility. It has large, crowded wards with little privacy. The new hospital is planned to open in 2027. It will care for children with conditions such as depression, autism, and ADHD.

This was the second time Bloom achieved this record. In 2025, the group brought together 10,000 people around a 1.7-mile table made from recycled materials. That event was in Alba Iulia, Romania. It focused on bringing people together and raising environmental awareness.

Bloom plans to recycle the materials from the latest table again. This time, they will be used to make children's furniture.
why_it_matters: The meal brought people together, raised money for children's mental health care, and used materials that Bloom plans to recycle again.
